title: The EB-1A vs EB-2 NIW Explained: Requirements, Criteria, and Qualification Strategies
summary: Compare EB-1A and EB-2 NIW requirements and criteria to see which green card path fits your background, evidence and achievements.
body_markdown:
## The EB-1A vs EB-2 NIW Explained


**EB-1A (Extraordinary Ability):** For people with sustained national or international acclaim. Self-petition; no job offer or PERM. Qualify via a single major award or 3 of 10 criteria, then clear final-merits review on the totality of evidence.


**EB-2 NIW (National Interest Waiver):** For those with an advanced degree or exceptional ability whose endeavor benefits the United States. Self-petition; no job offer or PERM. Must meet the EB-2 threshold and pass the Matter of Dhanasar three-prong test.


**Rule of thumb:** EB-1A turns on your elite recognition; NIW turns on the national importance of your work and your ability to advance it.


### EB-1A Green Card at a Glance


**Who it is for:** People at the very top of their field in science, business, tech, arts, or athletics.


**How you qualify:** (1) a one-time, major, internationally recognized award, or (2) at least 3 of 10 regulatory criteria plus a favorable final-merits determination.


**Why it is attractive:** Self-petition, no PERM, a priority category that often moves faster in the[monthly Visa Bulletin](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/legal/visa-law0/visa-bulletin.html) , and strong portability for founders and researchers. EB-1A eligibility is open to all five statutory fields, and the EB-1A visa requirements center on documented acclaim rather than a specific job.


### EB-1A Criteria: The 10 Regulatory Factors


The EB-1A extraordinary ability classification at 8 C.F.R. 204.5(h)(3) uses 10 criteria to evaluate your record. You need 3 or more of the criteria below (or a major award), then you must pass a final-merits review showing your recognition is set apart and sustained.


1. Lesser nationally or internationally recognized awards. Docs: certificates, selection criteria, number of competitors, press coverage.
2. Selective memberships requiring outstanding achievements. Docs: bylaws proving achievement-based admission, acceptance notices.
3. Published material about you in major media or top trade outlets. Docs: articles, interviews, circulation or traffic metrics, independent authorship.
4. Judging the work of others. Docs: peer-review invitations and completions, program committee roles, hackathon judging.
5. Original contributions of major significance. Docs: adoption letters from third parties, production use, patents implemented, standards impact.
6. Authorship of scholarly articles. Docs: publications list, citations, field-norm context.
7. Artistic exhibitions or showcases. Docs: curated programs, catalogs, gallery prestige evidence.
8. Leading or critical role for distinguished organizations. Docs: org prestige (press, funding, customers) plus your role's outcomes.
9. High salary or remuneration. Docs: contracts, W-2 or 1099, credible market benchmarks.
10. Commercial success in the performing arts. Docs: box office, streams, sales charts.


#### Final-Merits Tips


Tell a coherent elite-status story explaining why your recognition is rare compared to peers. Prefer independent validation (press, citations, third-party adoption) over internal praise. Map every exhibit to a specific criterion and to the final-merits narrative.


### EB-2 NIW Green Card at a Glance


The[EB-2 National Interest Waiver](https://www.legalos.ai/post/eb2-niw-guide) is designed for individuals with advanced education or exceptional ability. The EB-2 NIW green card pathway waives the employer sponsorship and PERM labor certification requirement when your work benefits the United States. It is one of the most accessible self-petition options for skilled professionals.


#### EB-2 Eligibility Requirements


EB-2 has two qualifying pathways. You must meet at least one:


- **Advanced Degree Pathway:** Hold a U.S. advanced degree (master's or doctorate) or equivalent foreign degree, or a U.S. bachelor's degree plus 5 years of progressive experience in your field.
- **Exceptional Ability Pathway:** Satisfy 3 of 6 indicators: (1) an academic degree related to the field, (2) 10+ years of full-time experience letters, (3) a license or certification to practice, (4) a high salary demonstrating exceptional ability, (5) membership in professional associations, or (6) recognition for achievements and contributions by peers, government entities, or professional organizations. Comparable evidence is allowed when the standard criteria do not fit the field.


#### The Dhanasar Three-Prong Test


Meeting the EB-2 threshold is only step one. To secure the NIW, your petition must pass the three-prong test from Matter of Dhanasar, 26 I&N Dec. 884 (AAO 2016), codified in the[USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 6, Part F, Chapter 5](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-6-part-f-chapter-5) :


1. **Substantial Merit and National Importance:** Your endeavor must have substantial merit and considerable intrinsic value to the United States. National importance can be regional or sector-specific when the work serves priorities of national concern.
2. **Well-Positioned to Advance the Endeavor:** Demonstrated through education, skills, prior record of success, concrete plans, progress already made, and interest from customers, users, investors, or institutions.
3. **On Balance, Beneficial to Waive Job Offer and PERM:** Waiving the job offer and PERM requirements must be in the national interest, supported by evidence like government endorsements, academic backing, or industry validation.


Dhanasar remains the controlling framework in 2026, but USCIS adjudicators are applying it more strictly. Theoretical arguments no longer suffice; each prong needs concrete, documented proof.


#### NIW Evidence Themes That Work


Frame the petition as Problem, Solution, Impact with U.S.-specific data. Include a roadmap with milestones for 12 to 24 months. Provide external validators: pilots, letters from independent stakeholders, grants, and customers. Articulate your comparative advantage: why you versus the alternatives.


### EB-1A vs EB-2 NIW: Choosing the Right Path


#### Which Category Fits Your Profile?


**Choose EB-1A if:**


- You can document 3 to 5 strong criteria from the 10-factor test.
- Your professional acclaim is widely recognized through major media coverage, prestigious awards, or selective memberships.
- You have sustained, elite-level recognition in your field.


**Choose EB-2 NIW if:**


- Your work addresses a clear national need, even if personal recognition is still growing.
- You hold an advanced degree or can document exceptional ability.
- Your endeavor delivers demonstrable value to the United States through research, public health, business solutions, or similar contributions.


**Dual-Track Strategy:** Many applicants file EB-1A and EB-2 NIW concurrently to hedge risk and maximize approval odds. If EB-1A approves, you can withdraw the NIW. If only the NIW approves, you still have a path to a green card.


Not sure which path fits?[LegalOS](https://www.legalos.ai/) can evaluate your profile against both criteria sets and recommend the strongest filing strategy.


### EB-1A for Software Engineers and Tech Professionals


Software engineers and technology professionals can pursue EB-1A by documenting elite recognition in their field.[O-1A-caliber evidence](https://www.legalos.ai/post/navigating-o-1a-visa-eligibility-essential-criteria-for-startup-founders) often maps directly to EB-1A: judging and standards work, adoption metrics showing impact, independent visibility in tech communities, and compensation exceeding industry norms.


Building a strong EB-1A case in tech often involves open-source contributions with significant adoption, speaking at major conferences, technical publications, and showing that your work has influenced industry standards. EB-2 NIW is also viable for software engineers when the work addresses a clear national need such as AI safety, cybersecurity infrastructure, or healthcare technology, even when personal recognition is still emerging.


### Building Your EB-1A Evidence: A 90-Day Framework


Strong EB-1A petitions come from organized, systematic evidence gathering.[LegalOS](https://www.legalos.ai/) can help you map your profile to the right criteria and build a petition strategy from day one. The 90-day sprint below provides a structured approach.


#### Weeks 1 to 3: Audit and Planning


Map your profile to the EB-1A criteria and Dhanasar; pick a primary track. Inventory existing evidence against the 10 criteria. Identify gaps and prioritize which criteria you will target. Secure 5 to 7 independent letters from customers, editors, PIs, standards leads, and C-suite contacts at partner organizations. Accept 3 to 5 judging or peer-review opportunities.


#### Weeks 4 to 6: Create Tangible Artifacts


Publish one high-signal artifact: a whitepaper, standards draft, open-source release, or accepted demo. Collect adoption metrics: deployments, user counts, revenue, outcomes, and security certifications. Develop visible proof of impact through a portfolio of projects, case studies, or open-source repositories. This phase targets criterion 3 (published material about you) and criterion 5 (original contributions of major significance).


#### Weeks 7 to 9: Demonstrate Traction and Proof


Land targeted trade coverage or thought-leadership placements. Collect metrics showing real-world impact: downloads, citations, media mentions, speaking invitations, or industry adoption. Consolidate salary and compensation proofs with credible market benchmarks. Secure letters from independent references and industry leaders.


#### Weeks 10 to 12: Assemble and Polish


Draft a personal or endeavor statement (the EB-1A final-merits narrative or the NIW roadmap). Build a tabbed exhibit index so each exhibit maps to a specific criterion or Dhanasar prong. Organize evidence into a cohesive, narrative-driven petition. Proofread and prepare for submission.


### EB-1A and EB-2 NIW Filing Mechanics


Both EB-1A and EB-2 NIW are filed using[USCIS Form I-140](https://www.uscis.gov/i-140) (Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker). Unlike most employment-based categories, both allow[self-petition](https://www.legalos.ai/post/how-to-self-petition-eb2-niw-visa-without-employer) , so you file on your own behalf without an employer.


The I-140 base filing fee is $715. A separate Asylum Program Fee also applies: $300 for self-petitioners, and $600 for employer-filed petitions by organizations with 26 or more employees (reduced rates apply to small employers and nonprofits). Verify current amounts on the[USCIS Fee Calculator](https://www.uscis.gov/feecalculator) before filing.


After I-140 approval, you file Form I-485 (Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status), either concurrently with the I-140 or sequentially depending on visa availability. With the I-485, you can also submit Form I-765 (Employment Authorization) and Form I-131 (Advance Parole). Premium processing is available for both EB-1A and EB-2 NIW. As of 2026 the premium processing fee is $2,965. USCIS targets 15 business days for EB-1A and 45 business days for EB-2 NIW.


For applicants outside the United States, consular processing at a U.S. embassy follows I-140 approval, with the visa interview handled abroad. Premium processing speeds only the I-140; it does not accelerate the I-485. Always check current visa availability and your EB-2 NIW priority date or EB-1A priority date for your country of chargeability in the monthly[Visa Bulletin](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/legal/visa-law0/visa-bulletin.html) .


Standard processing times in 2026 have widened. EB-1A I-140 adjudication ranges roughly 4 to 22 months depending on service center, and EB-2 NIW adjudication can run 12 to 24 months or longer. I-485 adjustment of status runs an additional 11 to 32 months. Confirm current ranges on the[USCIS Processing Times page](https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times/) . EB-1A and EB-2 NIW cost includes the I-140 filing fee, the Asylum Program Fee, any premium processing fee, and associated legal and evidence-preparation expenses. Note that[USCIS now requires ACH or card payments](https://www.legalos.ai/post/uscis-ach-payments-fees) (paper checks are being phased out). USCIS does not publish official EB-1A approval rate or EB-2 NIW approval rate figures, though practitioners have reported tightening NIW adjudication under the current stricter Dhanasar application.
